## Natural history notes

A medium-sized owlet moth characterized by mottled brown, gray, and tan wings with bold wavy lines and graphic, bark-like patterning that helps it blend into tree trunks and dead leaves. In Florida, it is found in hammocks, forests, pine flatwoods, parks, gardens, forest edges, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats with host plants and sheltered resting sites. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on woody plants and contribute to the food web as prey for birds, bats, spiders, and other insect-eating animals.
